papers_read.title_as_printed: Deep learning-based classification of healthy aging controls, mild cognitive impairment and Alzheimer's disease using fusion of MRI-PET imaging (Rallabandi & Seetharaman, 2023, doi 10.1016/j.bspc.2022.104312, file S1746809422007662)
Machine learning approaches to mild cognitive impairment detection based on structural MRI data and morphometric features (Zubrikhina et al., Cognitive Systems Research 78 (2023) 87-95)

what_each_reports.P-117: The record's P-117 (summaries.md S1746809423005462: resting-state EEG, VMD + NSGA-II, best ~99.8% accuracy, sample not reported) could not be checked; the pack PDF is a different paper (OASIS MRI-PET fusion, 95.5% HC vs MCI accuracy, AUC 0.988, internal 60/20/20 split).
what_each_reports.P-99: FreeSurfer morphometric features from structural MRI, SVC with chi-squared feature selection, 10-fold CV, Moscow Memory Clinic cohort of 207 (62 HC, 145 MCI). Accuracy 0.73 +/- 0.059, ROC-AUC 0.735, F1-macro 0.683.

quantity_a: Record's P-117: EEG classifier accuracy, MCI vs healthy, own cohort, internal validation (summary block only).
quantity_b: P-99: structural-MRI morphometry SVC accuracy, MCI vs HC, 207 Moscow participants, 10-fold CV.
incompatible_if_same: Not determinable and not needed; different modality and cohort. Two methods each reporting their own accuracy, neither claiming an ordering the other refutes.

gates.dataset_family: mismatch: Moscow Mental-health Clinic No. 1 cohort vs P-117's EEG cohort (or OASIS under the pack PDF); record's dataset_equal='Yes' unsupported
gates.modality_family: mismatch for the EEG paper the record means (structural MRI vs EEG); against the pack PDF's MRI-PET fusion the family would partly overlap, but the dataset gate still fails; no waiver on record

endpoint_and_metric: compatible metric type (accuracy, MCI vs control) but different cohorts and input modalities
performance_validity: Likely applies to P-117 (claimed 99.81% internal; the mapped MRI-PET PDF also reports AUC 0.985-0.989 on an internal split) but unconfirmable for the intended paper; not needed for the verdict.
grounds: The supplied P-117 PDF is the wrong paper (OASIS MRI-PET fusion), so the 99.81% EEG result cannot be checked from source.
The dataset-family gate fails under either identity of P-117 (Moscow memory-clinic cohort vs another cohort), and the modality gate fails for the EEG paper the record means; no waiver on record.
P-99's 73% is correctly quoted but is a structural-MRI morphometry accuracy in a different population, not a competing estimate of P-117's quantity.

evidence_quotes.quote: we used 60 % training, 20 % for validation and the remaining 20 % as a test set using various convolutional neural networks.
They proposed VMD-based EEG feature extraction with multi-objective channel optimization (NSGA variants) and supervised ML to detect MCI from resting-state EEG.
The dataset for the study consists of 62 healthy volunteers and 145 patients with MCI obtained from the «Memory Clinic» (Moscow, Russia).
We propose a machine learning method, which achieved an accuracy of 73%
the best and most stable results were obtained by SVC (0.68 F1, 0.735 ROC -AUC)

record_defects: P-117's paper_pdf_map entry points to the wrong PDF (MRI-PET S1746809422007662 instead of EEG S1746809423005462).
Registry row P-99 Dataset 'not reported' although the PDF names the Mental-health clinic No. 1 (Moscow) Memory Clinic cohort.
Registry row P-117: Best_Metric and Dataset 'not reported' despite the 99.81% claim.
resolution_note's bridging list is boilerplate unrelated to either paper.
what_would_change_the_verdict: The correct P-117 PDF would settle performance validity; it could not make the pair commensurable, since the cohorts differ and no waiver is on record.
